To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

glucocorticoid signaling is required for adipogenesis in vitro and that this requirement can be uncoupled from the requirement for other DIM components, such that treatment of 3T-3-L1 pre-adipocytes with glucocorticoids for 2 days followed by treatment with IBMX and FBS is sufficient to induce terminal differentiation of preadipocytes into mature adipocytes.
glucocorticoid signaling is a critical step in adipocyte commitment, and that glucocorticoidal induction of Pref-1 repression in preadipocyte cells is an important step in adipogenesis.

glucocorticoid signaling drives preadipocytes through a novel cellular state, the dexamethasones-primed pre-adipocyte, and that preadipocyte-factor 1 (Pref- 1) repression may be a determinant in this process.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular mechanisms that regulate adipocyte differentiation, with a special focus on the role of the adipogenic transcription factors C/EBPs and PPARgamma in the regulation of gene expression during adipocyte development.

the molecular basis of adipogenesis in vitro and in vivo, the molecular basis of the anti-obesity effect of glucocorticoid hormones, and the molecular basis of insulin resistance and lipolysis in obesity and diabetes.
the mechanisms of differentiation of adipose precursor cells, the molecular basis of insulin action, and the regulation of lipid metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sequential glucocorticoid and phosphodiesterase inhibitors treatment is a novel method for inducing adipogenesis in vitro and the glucocorticoid signaling is a key step in the adipogenic differentiation process in vitro.
glucocorticoid signaling induces preadipocytes into a novel intermediate state during adipogenesis.
the glucocorticoid-induced repression of the adipocyte inhibitor Pref-1 is a critical event in the commitment of mesenchymal precursor cells to the adipocyte lineage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glucocorticoids are the first and most critical factor in the adipocyte differentiation process.
the glucocorticoids play a crucial role in the early stages of adipogenesis.
glucocorticoid signaling is a critical component for commitment to the adipogenic lineage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glucocorticoid receptor (GR) signaling plays an important role in driving the commitment of mesenchymal progenitor cells to the adipocyte lineage in vitro.
glucocorticoid treatment of preadipocytes is sufficient to drive them to an intermediate adipogenic state that is characterized by repression of Pref-1, a key negative regulator of adipogenesis.
the sequential treatment with dexamethasome and IBMX is sufficient to induce adipogenesis, but treatment in the reverse order does not.
